title: Institutional name
before: Page titles use “Network Stimulation Laboratory”.
after: NetStim — Institute for Network Stimulation
why: Change the formal page title. Keep “lab” in ordinary prose.
references: NIMLab / Center for Brain Circuit Therapeutics

Explains the scientific approach in steps and separates it from institutional history. Useful for research structure. The lab identifies its home as Brigham and Women’s, within Mass General Brigham; it should not be labelled an MGH lab.

title: Opening
before: The homepage starts with a salutation; Cologne is already correct.
after:
Institute for Network Stimulation

We study how brain networks respond to stimulation and how these responses relate to neurological and psychiatric symptoms. Our group is based at University Hospital Cologne. We use structural and functional MRI, diffusion imaging and computational modelling to investigate these questions.

Together with collaborators, we develop Lead-DBS, an open-source toolbox for reconstructing DBS electrodes and modelling stimulation from postoperative MRI and CT images.
why: Use the institute name as the heading. Describe the research and methods underneath. The original welcome could also stay; a new slogan is unnecessary. Scope and methods come from the NetStim pages reviewed, not from the reference labs.
references: Names the questions, then describes how the group investigates them. This is the strongest model for the NetStim research page.
Names methods and research aims, with uncertainty about what the work may lead to. Publications are identified as papers or preprints.
Moves from the research aim to the recordings used to investigate it. Use that specificity; the page’s older news is not a model for currency.

after: Keep the heading “Publications”. Add a small selection of papers above the full list, with authors, title, journal and year. Label preprints. The journal list can be shortened once the papers are in place.
why: The problem is that readers cannot readily see the work. There is no need to replace the section with promotional summaries.
references: Names methods and research aims, with uncertainty about what the work may lead to. Publications are identified as papers or preprints.

title: Funding

title: Research framing
before: “cognitive disorders such as Depression” groups unlike conditions together.
after:
We investigate how the location of deep brain stimulation and its connections to other brain regions relate to clinical outcomes. We reconstruct electrode locations from postoperative imaging and use structural and functional connectivity to study the networks associated with improvement in symptoms.

Our work also asks how stimulation of a small brain region affects activity across a wider network.
why: State the scientific questions and how they are studied. In the retained condition list, replace the category that places depression under cognitive disorders; confirm which conditions represent the group’s present focus.
references: Names the questions, then describes how the group investigates them. This is the strongest model for the NetStim research page.
